source.title: Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders
source.authors: F. Nooralahzadeh; Lea Bogensperger; C. Bluethgen; M. Krauthammer

record.tranche_reason: The study measures sparse clinical-finding information in embedding channels, but does not test whether individual neurons respond to several unrelated inputs or whether apparent mixtures have a shared feature.
record.gate_note: The paper reports channel selectivity, sparse-probe performance, and ablation effects. These concern related representation properties, but none directly measures polysemantic responses as defined in the claim. Results from cited studies and report-generation metrics are not included as claim rows.
record.test_reason: The study ranks final-embedding coordinates of frozen 3D CT encoders (Pillar-0, Merlin) by per-finding AUROC, fits sparse probes and ablates channels. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. It never tests superposition, capacity, architecture or measurement effects on polysemanticity. Superposition (Elhage et al. 2022) is only cited in related work. Its results concern sparse, selective readout of clinical findings, a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that frozen 3D CT encoders store findings in sparse, causally selective channel subsets, with partial overlap among related findings. The probe recipe transfers across hospitals and backbones when anatomy matches.
record.recipe_differences: Uses selectivity-ranked embedding coordinates, closed-form probes, and channel ablation in frozen 3D medical encoders; it does not use the original neuron-visualization method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies top-K and datasets/backbones/anatomy; it reports that K=10 performs near full-dimensional probes and that transfer degrades with anatomy mismatch. These are not tests of polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: Clinical findings are decodable from about 10 embedding coordinates each. Ablation is selective: 0.0060 on-target vs 0.00003 off-target AUROC drop. Some coordinates recur across related findings in Table 5 (e.g. 897 and 792 across calcification, cardiomegaly and mosaic attenuation).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In frozen 3D CT encoders, findings are read out from sparse, selectively necessary embedding coordinates, with some coordinates shared among anatomically related findings.

record.problems: The study does not measure single-channel responses across unrelated input types, so its sparse clinical probes and ablations cannot determine how often channels are polysemantic. The authors note higher-variance channel estimates for rare findings.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted classification and report-generation comparisons that concern detector or verbalizer performance rather than channel polysemanticity; also omitted cited baseline results.

untested.parts: No single-unit response analysis across unrelated input types. Subjects are final embedding coordinates of 3D medical encoders, not classifier neurons.
No test of feature count versus dimension or of superposition as a cause.
No test of initialization, regularization or noise.
No comparison of polysemanticity across activation functions or architectures.
No variation of activation range or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The paper only cites superposition work and does not discuss polysemanticity. Channel reuse across findings in Table 5 might look like multi-finding coordinates, but the paper does not analyze it as polysemanticity. The shared findings are mostly clinically related, and the coordinates are final contrastive embedding dimensions, so no row should link to V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether individual image-classifier neurons respond to several unrelated input types.
No language models or transformer MLP neurons are studied.
Does not measure feature count relative to neuron capacity or test superposition as a cause.
Does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.
Does not compare activation functions or architectures for polysemanticity, or measure a polysemanticity-performance tradeoff.
Does not investigate canonical polysemantic neurons or test whether apparently unrelated inputs share a feature.
Does not vary the activation range examined or compare explanation-scoring methods for polysemanticity.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed each finding's dev-ranked top-K=10 embedding channels and recomputed probe AUROCs.
rows.measure: Mean AUROC drop on the targeted finding versus mean drop on other findings
rows.value: Mean on-target drop 0.0060; mean off-target drop 0.00003 (∼20× difference)
rows.locator: Analysis and discussion, Causal ablation; Figure 3
rows.note: The authors describe selective necessity for the finding's probe score; this does not test whether a channel responds to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: Probe AUROC drop after ablating selected channels. It shows selective necessity, not whether a channel responds to unrelated inputs. The reader's 'observed' state only holds relative to the paper's own claim, not any version.

rows.subject: Pillar-0
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean test AUROC using the per-finding top-K channels with the full embedding.
rows.measure: Mean test AUROC of clinical-finding probes
rows.locator: Analysis and discussion, Each finding lives in ∼10 channels; Figure 2
rows.note: Sparse probe performance is evidence about channel encoding of clinical findings, not a measurement of polysemanticity.
rows.check: Compares the study's own sparse probe with the full-embedding probe. This is method performance, not a polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: Merlin
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap among category-level top-10 channel circuits.
rows.measure: Cross-category Jaccard overlap of channel circuits
rows.locator: Analysis and discussion, Merlin circuits by clinical category; Figure 4
rows.note: The text also reports near-zero overlap for liver versus lower thorax, without an exact value. This is category-circuit overlap, not evidence about individual channels' responses to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: Category-level Jaccard overlap of selected channel sets. Overlap arises where anatomy is related, so it cannot show mixing of unrelated inputs in single units.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
